reason: Montenegro shows the core of Moldova's problem in another form: in 2023 an independent assessment found that a system under implementation since January 2021 needed substantial upgrading and that old technology limited further upgrading, as the Commission finds MTender outdated, and both countries rely on external funds. But Montenegro upgraded the system rather than replacing it, and a search of all 204 Montenegrin evidence passages in the project for procurement terms found none showing the technology limit removed, gaps in procedures or stages set out in law, or any effect on centralised procurement. The case therefore shows a recently introduced system judged technically limited and then improved, not an outdated system being replaced.

North Macedonia's integrated system is described by the Commission as functioning efficiently in every report from 2021 to 2026, and the version launched on 1 April 2025 is an update of a working system; a search of all 4,629 passages in the North Macedonian evidence files found none saying the earlier system was outdated or inadequate. The case matches the state Moldova is aiming for, an obligatory system adapted to the procurement law, rather than Moldova's problem, and the Commission's limited progress finding leaves the content and effect of the update unknown. It does not show an outdated system being replaced.

Agent synthesis, not stated by a source: an independent assessment of the electronic system, requested by the procurement policy body and used to direct EU or donor funds, could work in Moldova, which already has funding from international partners and World Bank review of its procurement documents. The condition is that such a review reaches the technology choice of the new system before it is built, since Montenegro's system was judged to rest on old technology within about two years of its start. The upgrade route itself does not transfer, because Moldova is replacing MTender and the case gives no evidence that Montenegro's upgrade worked.

Agent synthesis, not stated by a source: adapting the system to the procurement law, making its use obligatory for all contracting authorities and adding modules in stages under one responsible body could serve Moldova, whose Reform Agenda pilot already starts with essential modules. The condition is that Moldova first has a working new core system, since the North Macedonian case shows the upgrading of a sound system and nothing on replacing an outdated one. Contract management, which MTender lacks, is not among the stages listed for North Macedonia.

The World Bank stated in 2023 that the system had been under implementation since January 2021, and the Commission reports improvements implemented in 2023 to 2024 and in 2024 to 2025. A search of all 204 Montenegrin evidence passages in the project for procurement terms found no figure on use and no statement that use is obligatory or covers every procedure, so in_practice is not supported, and none states whether the EU-funded upgrade was delivered.

The assessment started in January 2023 and included a dedicated three-day review of the e-procurement system, and the Commission states that the MAPS project ended in December 2023 with a comprehensive evaluation focused on electronic procurement. Only the World Bank's interim slides are available in a usable form, so the final report's findings are unknown.

The Commission states that improved functionalities of the system facilitate the monitoring of contract award, implementation and appeals, but the sentence describes what the system enables and gives no measure of monitoring or of use. A search of all 204 Montenegrin evidence passages in the project for procurement terms found no other measure of a result of the system.

The only statement of the outcome describes what the system's improved functions enable and gives no measure, and a search of all 204 Montenegrin evidence passages in the project for procurement terms found no measure of monitoring or use. There is therefore no observed outcome to which the system's contribution could be attributed.
